body:
## Pull request overview

This PR fixes critical filter operator bugs in the ObjectStack spec and memory driver. The root cause was that `parseFilterAST()` converts AST operators to `$`-prefixed FilterCondition format (e.g., `$contains`), but the memory driver's `convertToMongoQuery()` previously had a passthrough branch that sent these directly to Mingo, which doesn't understand non-standard operators like `$contains`, resulting in empty results for all string/range/null filters.

**Changes:**
- `filter.zod.ts` in `packages/spec`: Adds `$notContains` to `StringOperatorSchema`, `FieldOperatorsSchema`, `Filter<T>` type, `VALID_AST_OPERATORS`, `AST_OPERATOR_MAP`, and `FILTER_OPERATORS`
- `memory-driver.ts`: Replaces the Mingo passthrough with `normalizeFilterCondition()` and `normalizeFieldOperators()` that translate `$contains`, `$notContains`, `$startsWith`, `$endsWith`, `$between`, and `$null` to Mingo-native operators; also adds `notcontains`/`not_contains` to `convertConditionToMongo()`
- `memory-matcher.ts`: Adds `$notContains` and `$null` cases to `checkCondition()`; adds corresponding tests across `filter.test.ts` and `memory-driver.test.ts`

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| `packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts` | Adds `$notContains` operator to all relevant schemas, types, maps and constants |
| `packages/spec/src/data/filter.test.ts` | Adds tests for `$notContains` schema validation, AST parsing, and `isFilterAST` detection |
| `packages/plugins/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts` | Replaces Mingo passthrough with `normalizeFilterCondition` + `normalizeFieldOperators`; adds `notcontains`/`not_contains` to `convertConditionToMongo` |
| `packages/plugins/driver-memory/src/memory-matcher.ts` | Adds `$notContains` and `$null` cases to `checkCondition` |
| `packages/plugins/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.test.ts` | Adds 12 integration tests covering all new operators in FilterCondition object format |
</details>

In `normalizeFieldOperators`, the cases for `$contains`, `$startsWith`, and `$endsWith` all write to `result.$regex`. If a filter has more than one of these operators on the same field (e.g., `{ name: { $startsWith: 'A', $endsWith: 'n' } }`), the second operator silently overwrites the `$regex` set by the first. Only the last processed operator's regex pattern is applied, and the earlier constraints are lost. To fix this, each of these operators should be combined into a single regex (e.g., concatenating both `^` and `$` anchors into one expression), or this limitation should be documented.

In `checkCondition`, there is an early-return guard at line 106: `if (value === undefined && op !== '$exists' && op !== '$ne') { return false; }`. Because `$null` is not excluded from this guard, when a field is missing (`value === undefined`) and the operator is `$null: true`, the guard fires and returns `false` — meaning `$null: true` fails to match fields that don't exist on a record. Since `$null: true` is semantically "field is null or missing", the guard should also exclude `$null` (i.e., the condition should be `op !== '$exists' && op !== '$ne' && op !== '$null'`) so that the `$null` case in the switch can evaluate correctly for undefined values.

The test at line 680 is named `'should handle $contains inside $or'`, but the test body actually uses `$startsWith` inside the `$or` clause — not `$contains`. The description should be updated to `'should handle $startsWith inside $or'` to accurately reflect what is being tested.
